category_title: Seventh-grade students in an urban classroom exhibiting frequent off-task behavior
minimal_context: The student is seated at a table with peers in a social studies class, working on a map activity with their journal open.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please open your journals, make sure your pencils are sharpened, and begin working independently on your map activity at your tables.

STUDENT: See? My notebook is out, too. Am I doing a good job on my map?

TUTOR: Just keep working on it.

STUDENT: We need to go back to how she was doing class. You aren't saying anything when we do it right.

TUTOR: Don't worry about that right now, and don't talk to your neighbors. Just stay in your seat and finish the map.

STUDENT: (Stands up from the table and stops working on the map) I'm not doing this. (Walks over to another group to start a nonacademic conversation and begins eating a snack)

options.A: Leave the student free to choose any format and materials they like to complete the map activity at their table.
options.B: Concentrate on reducing negative statements, including reprimands and 'shh' sounds, to quiet the class down during the activity.
options.C: Instruct the student to open their journal, write their name and date, and write as much as they can recall about the map, reminding them to provide a full retelling rather than a summary.
options.D: Ask the student to respond to the map's features in their journal: How did the activity make them feel? What emotions did it evoke?
